title: OK depending on what you’re looking for
text:
TL;DR: the comics you get are NOT worth double the price as claimed by the seller but the subscription is fairly priced after considering costs involved in shipping and curating comics. Cheaper alternatives include TPBs and subscriptions from the publisher.

What I asked for: Daredevil, Batman, Superman

What I got: 2 outstanding Daredevil comics, #3 of 5 from a random Batman miniseries, a dollar bin Superman comic (Action Comics #999), the rest were B- and C- list comics including a comic that literally said “free” because it was a free comic book day issue.

Shipping: comics are not individually bagged and boarded but rather stacked together and shrink wrapped. As a result there is a minimum amount of creasing around the corners and spine, not enough to affect aesthetic appeal but collectors know even the smallest imperfections can have a significant impact on a comic’s value.

Value: based on previous sales on eBay, the comics I received were worth ~$14. I consider the subscription to be a fair price after considering the costs involved in shipping and having someone curate the comics for you, but by no measure (cover price or market value) were the comics worth “double the subscription cost” as claimed by comic garage.

Alternatives: if you want to read good comic stories, TPBs are among the cheapest way to do so. If you want comics with your favorite characters mailed to you monthly in an ongoing series, you can subscribe to ~12-18 different comic series direct from Marvel or DC for the price of a Comic’s Garage subscription over the course of the year. If you want to be surprised by a collection of random comics each month, Comics Garage might be for you.
label: neutral
